findings.why_it_matters: The PDF prints this as a numbered subsection heading of 2.1 (styled like 1.2.1 on page 857, which the markdown renders as '####'); here it is demoted to bold text, so the clause is invisible to heading-based navigation and section lookup.

The PDF prints 2.2 as a numbered section heading, a sibling of 2.1 (rendered '###' on page 857) and 2.3 (rendered as a heading on page 859); here it is demoted to bold text, so section 2.2 cannot be found by heading.

2.3 is a sibling of 2.1, which page 857 renders '### 2.1 FUNCTION DEFINITION AND RETURNED VALUE' under '## 2. GENERAL DESCRIPTION'; rendering 2.3 at '##' puts it at the level of the numbered clause 2, a wrong heading level that breaks the section hierarchy. The same holds for '## 2.4 DEFINITIONS OF FUNCTIONS' on this page.
2.4 is a sibling of 2.1 ('###' on page 857); at '##' it is rendered at the level of clause 2, a wrong heading level.

findings.pdf_says:
A means alphabetic

findings.markdown_says:
A means alphabetic
I means integer
N means numeric
X means alphanumeric
findings.why_it_matters: The PDF prints the Arguments-column and Type-column code legends as one entry per line; the markdown writes them as consecutive lines with no list markup or line breaks, so rendered Markdown joins each legend into one run-on line ('A means alphabetic I means integer N means numeric X means alphanumeric'). The text survives in the source but the printed list structure is lost when rendered.
